# Throughline candidates

Seeded from the critical-analysis inventory. Pick one with `continue --pick TLN`.

## Candidate TL1 — Δfur is the demonstrable driver of phage susceptibility

**Claim.** Loss of the ferric-uptake regulator (Δfur) is the single
demonstrable driver of the phage-susceptibility phenotype.

**Evidence chain.** The Δfur knockout shows a 4.1× shift in plaque-forming
efficiency (fig 3); the effect reverses on complementation; regulon analysis
ties it to three susceptibility genes. This is the claim the data most
directly supports.

**Arc.** TL1 → mechanism → the two confirming figures → implications.

## Candidate TL2 — Iron-limitation reprograms the phage-defense regulon

**Claim.** Iron limitation reprograms a broad phage-defense regulon, of which
the fur effect is one arm.

**Evidence chain.** Leans on the transcriptomic survey (fig 5) more than the
knockout. More novel-sounding, less airtight — two regulon genes have an
ambiguous direction of effect.

**Arc.** Best where the audience rewards breadth over a single clean result.

## Candidate TL3 — A two-gene switch gates the whole susceptibility phenotype

**Claim.** A two-gene epistatic switch gates the entire susceptibility
phenotype.

**Evidence chain.** Tightest, most provocative, but the second gene's role
rests on a single un-replicated epistasis experiment (fig 6). A sharp
reviewer will press on n=1.

**Arc.** Reserve for a venue where the provocative framing is worth the risk.
